samples.summary: The cell-rectangle shape keeps a read/write asymmetry that contradicts the change's own stated principle. `visitStyledRunsInRange` (model/range-runs.ts) *auto-dispatches* on `range.tableCellRange` to `visitCellRectangleSlices`, but the write, `Doc.applyInlineStyle`, deliberately ignores `tableCellRange` and requires every caller to route to the new `applyInlineStyleToCells` by hand. That is exactly the "agreement by convention rather than by construction" the whole refactor is justified by (see docs-font-controls.md's new "The shared range traversal" section and the task's lesson "A contract a function documents is only as good as its callers"), and it is the contract that already produced two shipped bugs (Cmd+\ and Cmd+Alt+V restyling the whole table). The diff fixes the current callers and adds a per-editor routing helper, but leaves the footgun in the model: any future call of `applyInlineStyle` with a rectangle-shaped selection silently restyles every cell of the table (e.g. the link paths in view/editor.ts around lines 2948/2983 only work because a manual `if (range.tableCellRange)` guard precedes them). Dispatching the rectangle inside `applyInlineStyle` — mirroring the read — would make the agreement structural for all four selection shapes rather than three.
samples.evidence: document.ts applyInlineStyle doc comment: "A `range.tableCellRange` is ignored here, as it always was: the editors route a cell rectangle to `applyStyleToCellRange` above this call." vs range-runs.ts: "if (range.tableCellRange) { visitCellRectangleSlices(...); return; }"

samples.summary: The new architecture is recorded only in docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md (a toolbar/font-controls doc), while the canonical subsystem docs for the behaviours it changes are untouched and now partly contradict the code: (a) docs-pending-inline-style.md:57-61 still states the collapsed-caret contract as "read the *visual* style (caret style + any existing pending merged) so re-toggles flip the displayed state", whereas `TextEditor.toggleStyle` now decides from `effectiveVisual` (named-style defaults layered in) while storing raw; (b) docs-named-styles.md's "Cascade resolution model" is the canonical home of the "reads resolve the cascade / writes store raw runs" rule the diff makes load-bearing, and gains no mention; (c) docs.md's `Doc` method table (line 129) and its src/model file tree list `applyInlineStyle` but not the newly added public `Doc.applyInlineStyleToCells` or the three new model modules. Per CONTRIBUTING/docs/design/README the repo files docs by subsystem and expects the canonical doc to be folded into rather than a second doc carrying the material.
searchedFor: read docs/design/docs/docs.md lines 115-145 and 275-301 (Doc method table + file tree)
samples.evidence: docs-pending-inline-style.md:57-61 "Both surfaces share the same collapsed-caret contract: they read the *visual* style (caret style + any existing pending merged)" — the diff changes that decision input to the effective style.

samples.summary: Scope declared out of scope is shipped anyway, and the task doc was not updated. docs/tasks/active/20260810-docs-range-aware-toggles-todo.md:93-95 lists under "Out of scope": "The header/footer slim toggles' `pressed` state: those `Toggle`s were already uncontrolled before this change (no `pressed` prop at all), so wiring them is a separate fix." The diff nevertheless adds `pressed={isStyleOn(slimSummary?.bold/italic/underline)}` plus a new `slimSummary` read and dedicated regression tests for the pressed state. The change itself is defensible (the lessons file argues state and action must share a source), but the spec of record still says otherwise — one of the two should be reconciled so reviewers can tell intended scope from drift.

samples.summary: A behaviour change reaches the slides text-formatting surface without its design doc being reconciled. The text-box editor's `getSelectionStyle` / `getRangeStyleSummary` / `stepSelectionFontSize` now report the *effective* style, so a run with no explicit size in a heading block reports the named-style size (the new test asserts `fontSize === 11` and `color === '#666666'` for heading-6). slides-toolbar-redesign.md:253 still describes the Size picker as "resolved via `getRangeStyleSummary()` with `DEFAULT_INLINE_STYLE.fontSize` as the fallback for unset runs", which is no longer how unset runs resolve inside a styled block. Reasonable behaviour, but it is unrequested scope relative to issue #715's stated approach ("switching the toggles to the summary is a no-op for carets and a fix for ranges") and the doc now describes the old resolution.
samples.evidence: slides-toolbar-redesign.md:253 "Value resolved via `getRangeStyleSummary()` with `DEFAULT_INLINE_STYLE.fontSize` as the fallback for unset runs."

samples.summary: The consolidation stops one file short of the caret-seam walk it duplicates. `model/color.ts`'s `resolveColorAtPosition` implements the identical `offset <= inlineEnd` seam scan (its own comment says it uses "the standard … rule used by `getStyleAtCursor` / `getSelectionStyle`"), and `view/link-run.ts:36-41` carries a third variant. Given the change's premise that copies of this walk drift, the new `model/caret-style.ts` is a natural place for a shared "inline at caret" primitive these could resolve through.
samples.evidence: color.ts:50-55 comment: "with the standard 'cursor at the seam between two inlines belongs to the leading inline' rule used by `getStyleAtCursor` / `getSelectionStyle`" — the same loop caret-style.ts now owns.

verdict.reason: The quoted code is genuinely present (document.ts:357-365 contract comment; range-runs.ts:76-80 read-side auto-dispatch; editor.ts:2940 manual guard before the link write), but it is not blocking under the design-fit rubric. (a) The originating task's acceptance items for the cell rectangle (todo lines 67-78) are met: the rectangle read (range-runs.ts:77) and the rectangle write (document.ts:377 applyInlineStyleToCells) both drive the same visitCellRectangleSlices, so read/write agreement on which cells are covered IS structural for that shape; the objection is to the entry-point shape, not to a second traversal. (b) The contract is a deliberate, documented decision folded into the canonical design doc under "One write path per editor" (docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:379-391), so design-doc discipline is satisfied, not violated. (c) No current caller misbehaves — the finding itself concedes callers were fixed and the cited link paths are guarded — so this is hardening against hypothetical future callers, i.e. an API-taste/"could be cleaner" preference, which the rubric classifies as minor and explicitly never blocking. It is not duplication of an existing module, not a Non-Goal breach, and not a missing or parallel design doc.
